Sam: Proposal — enforce model-size slabs (small/medium/large/xlarge) with soft-burst credits per API key. Soft bursts should degrade to a cheaper model variant instead of returning 429s. Thoughts? :thinking:
Anya: Love the soft-fallback idea. Need to decide where to enforce soft vs hard: control plane policy vs runtime router?
Devon: Runtime router should handle soft fallback to keep latency down. Hard quotas (billing/contract limits) can be enforced at the control plane.
Priya: Operational concern: tracking per-key per-family token buckets at runtime means sharded state. We'll need a fast in-memory store for resilience (redis/rocksdb?). Cache misses could add ~1–3ms.
Sam: Sketch of config idea:
```
model_quota:
  key_scope: org_id
  families:
    - name: "text-base"
      slab: small
      burst_tokens: 5000
      sustained_tpm: 2000
    - name: "lm-70b"
      slab: xlarge
      burst_tokens: 1000
      sustained_tpm: 200
```
Devon: Suggest hybrid approach: local leaky bucket in the runtime with background sync to central ledger. Local fast path for enforcement, periodic reconciliation to control plane for accounting.
Priya: Telemetry requirements: emit per-model-family metrics: quota_hit_rate, burst_consumption, fallback_rate, local_bucket_fill. These drive dashboard tiles and regression alerts.
Anya: UX: console should expose remaining burst credits per API key and per route, plus an opt-in toggle for "allow soft fallback" and a histogram of fallback events. Also show which cheaper variant was used for each fallback.
Sam: Edge case: retry storms & spikey traffic. We should clamp short-lived spikes with a cooldown and surface Retry-After + X-Redwood-Fallback headers so clients can backoff or accept fallback.
Devon: Also propose small API tweak: add model_family param to the rate-limiter API so enforcement can be keyed by family. Example body: {"model_family":"lm-70b","tokens":512}.
Priya: Alerting: when fallback_rate > 2% sustained for 1h, page product on-call and notify the account owner. Also a daily report of soft-fallback volume per org.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout plan created: PR #4212. Soft-fallback feature toggles to be enabled for 10% of traffic in canary.
Devon: Performance notes: local token-bucket ops should be <200ns in hot path, redis only for long-tail reconciliation. Need benchmarks.
Lucy: Security / billing note: hard-enforced quotas (reserved capacity customers) must bypass soft fallback and always return 429 when exceeded. We should mark those orgs in control plane policy.
Anya: I'll mock console tiles and include a compact view for SREs (alerts / recent quota hits) and an expanded view for customers (per-key detail).
Sam: Action items:
- Sam -> open RFC + PR for runtime enforcement and API param (will include example config and sync protocol)
- Anya -> mock console tiles & Figma link
- Priya -> telemetry naming + dashboard prototypes (Grafana panels and alert rules)
- Devon -> design local token-bucket sync plan + perf numbers
- Lucy -> list of reserved-capacity orgs to mark as hard-enforce
Anya: I'll add mock screenshots in Figma and link here when ready.
Sam: OK, I'll file the RFC and tag infra + runtime teams. :+1:
